turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: What was your team's deployment frequency?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: We deployed about twice a day, on demand rather than on a schedule.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Which CI system were you using?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: GitHub Actions, with a self-hosted runner pool for the heavier jobs.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: What was the test coverage on that repo?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Around seventy percent on lines, higher on the core modules.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: How many services were in production?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Twenty-three, though about six of them were doing almost nothing.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Tell me about a project that did not go well.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: The search rewrite. We underestimated the relevance work and shipped something that was faster and worse, and we ended up reverting most of it.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Describe a time you mentored someone.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I onboarded two junior engineers last year, mostly by pairing with them on real tickets rather than giving them starter tasks.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Tell me about a technical decision you would make differently now.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Choosing a document store for data that turned out to be deeply relational. We spent a year working around it.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: How do you keep up with changes in the field?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Badly and on purpose. I read post-mortems and source code rather than news.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: What do you look for in a code review?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Whether I can tell what the change is trying to do without asking. Style comes second.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: What are you looking for in your next role?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: A team where the hard problem is the product rather than the deploy pipeline.
